issue: Arcom's English machine translation of art. 3 duplicated the cinema-channel sentence for cat. III and then said 'before 10 pm', leaving the service mapping ambiguous.
current_resolution: CLOSED 2026-11-06. Confirmed against the FRENCH text from two independent sources: Legifrance JORFTEXT000000446802 (the 2005 original) and the csa.fr consolidated page carrying the 'Modifiee par la deliberation n. 2014-17 du 5 mars 2014' banner. Both read identically: 'pour les chaines cinema et les services de paiement a la seance, ces programmes ne doivent pas etre diffuses le mercredi avant 20 h 30. issue: Working C-02 exposed a substantive extraction error of our own. Delib. 2014-17 replaced the fifth alinea of art. 2 and BROADENED the category III definition, but the table still carried the 2005 wording: 'leur scenario recourt de facon repetee ET SYSTEMATIQUE' became 'le programme recourt de facon repetee'.
current_resolution: CLOSED 2026-11-06. FR-CLS-003 now carries the current wording. The pre-2014 wording is retained as FR-CLS-903, status=superseded, valid_to=2014-04-08.
action_required: None for the rule itself. The lesson matters more: the error survived because the English translation and the pre-2014 French text AGREED with each other, so cross-source corroboration did not catch it - only reading the amending instrument did. Treat any source whose amendment history is not explicit as suspect, and always diff the amending deliberation rather than trusting a page labelled 'consolidated'.

issue: Only Code Sections One and Two had been reviewed. Sections Three to Ten were assumed irrelevant to age ratings and broadcast hours.
current_resolution: REVIEWED 2026-11-06. The assumption was mostly right but not entirely: Rule 4.7 (Religion) bars claims that a living person has special powers 'when significant numbers of children may be expected to be watching' - a child-audience broadcast restriction outside Section One. Added as UK-REL-001. Sections Three (crime, disorder, hatred, abuse), Five and Six (impartiality, elections), Seven and Eight (fairness, privacy) and Nine and Ten (commercial references) carry no age-rating or broadcast-hour restriction and stay out of scope.
action_required: Worth one more pass by a UK compliance reviewer to confirm nothing else in sections 3-10 keys off a child audience or a time of day. The pattern to look for is not the watershed but the phrase 'significant numbers of children'.
